title: The Power Of Starting Something Stupid

questions.q: What does Norton advise when friends call an idea stupid?
questions.why: He says hearing "stupid" should prompt you to listen to your instincts, as many great ideas were once dismissed.

questions.q: How should you break down a big, "stupid" idea?
a: Chunk it into smallest manageable projects
questions.why: He recommends chunking the idea into tiny projects to allow safe, small‑scale failure.

questions.q: What does Norton suggest you do with limited resources?
a: Use what you have and learn as you go
Wait until you can afford ideal tools
questions.why: He urges working with what you have, like selling ice cream from a kitchen window with a cheap maker.

questions.q: Which example illustrates a "stupid" idea that succeeded?
questions.why: The text uses iPads in restaurants as a brilliant yet initially dismissed concept.

questions.q: What mindset does Norton promote regarding societal "don'ts"?
questions.why: He encourages saying yes to ideas despite common discouragements.
